Hmm, wait, looking at the image: the token at around columns 27-30 shows light blue on the left, dark blue on the right. So the token's appearance changed — the b border is now on the right side.
Hmm, this is weird. Maybe the token is actually two separate 2x4 objects (a b block and an S block) that move together, and the rendering is… no, that's not it. Or maybe the token's "b" side faces the direction of…? Initially: b on left, S on right. After moving left 4 times: still b on left, S on right (23-24 b, 25-26 S). After RIGHT: S on left (27-28), b on right (29-30).
Wait, let me re-check the previous frame. Before RIGHT: token b (19,23,22,24), S (19,25,22,26). So b is 23-24, S is 25-26. After RIGHT: S (19,27,22,28), b (19,29,22,30). So S is 27-28, b is 29-30. The token moved 4 to the right (23→27), but the b and S swapped sides!
So the token flipped horizontally. Why? Maybe the token is like a "car" that flips when it changes direction? Or… the token is actually a 4x4 object with b on one side and S on the other, and it flipped because it moved right?
Hmm, or maybe the token is a "reflected" object: when it moves right, the b side faces right. When it moves left, the b side faces left. So the b side faces the direction of motion! Initially (before any movement) b was on the left… and it was moving left. After RIGHT, b is on the right. So the b border faces the direction of motion. Interesting but probably not important.
Now, what's the goal? Let me think about the overall picture:
- Top: a 5x5 blue square (left), a track with a 4x4 token that slides between columns 23-42 (blocked by the notch on the left).
- Bottom: a 9x9 square with a purple plus, a 17x17 square with a g/W checkerboard.
- Right edge: a green timer bar that shrinks with each step (currently about 55% of the height).
The timer is shrinking! I need to hurry. If the timer runs out → game over?
What could the goal be? Let me think: the purple plus in the small square and the checkerboard in the large square. Maybe the goal is to make the two squares "match" in some way. The token on the track is… hmm.
Wait — maybe this is a "pattern completion" game: the large square is a 3x3 grid of 5x5 cells (checkerboard: corners are g, edges are W, center is g). The small square is a 3x3 grid of 3x3 cells with a purple plus (center column + center row are purple… actually the plus is: top center, left center, right center, bottom center are purple; corners and center are g).
Hmm, if I map the small square's plus onto the large square's checkerboard… the large square has g at corners + center, W at edge centers. The small square has purple at edge centers, g at corners + center. So the small square's purple is where the large square has W! If the purple blocks "become" W… the small square's pattern (corners g, center g, edges purple) corresponds to the large square (corners g, center g, edges W). So the transformation is: purple → white.
Maybe the game is: the token is a "key" that, when placed at a specific position on the track, converts purple to white? Or the goal is to move the token to a specific position to complete the level?
Or maybe I'm overthinking this. Maybe the goal is simply: move the token all the way to the right end (42) or to a specific position, and that completes the level. The notch blocks the left side; the right end is the terminus.
Or the goal is: the token needs to be at a position where it "connects" the left square and the right end…
Let me look at the track: it spans 17-42. The left square is 12-16. The token's leftmost is 23-26 (blocked by the notch at 17-22). The token's rightmost is 39-42 (initial position).
Hmm, wait. Actually, maybe the notch isn't a blocker. Let me re-verify: when I pressed LEFT at the position where the token was 23-26, the board changed but the token didn't move (only the HUD). So yes, the notch is blocking.
Or the notch is where the token should "drop": maybe UP/DOWN moves the token vertically, and the notch is a hole the token can fall into? Let me test DOWN with the token at the notch position. First move the token left to 23-26, then press DOWN.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the notch is a gap in the track, and the token can't cross it because the track is broken there. But maybe the left square is the "goal" — the token should reach the left square. The notch prevents that… unless the token can jump/fall.
Or, maybe the puzzle is: the purple plus in the small square is a "key pattern" that needs to be inserted into the notch? The notch is 6 wide x 2 tall. Hmm, no.
Let me think about the sizes: the notch is 6 columns x 2 rows. The token is 4x4. The left square is 5x5.
Hmm, what if the goal is to make the top structure symmetric? Currently: left square (5x5) + track + token.
Let me try a different approach: test the vertical movement. Move the token to 23-26 (LEFT once), then press DOWN and UP to see if the token moves vertically or falls into the notch.
